subject: Mapping request: PII classification, access gaps, and export / transfer playbook
messages:
From: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@bioheal.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: dpo@bioheal.com, procure@bioheal.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 14:12:00 +0200
Subject: Request: PII handling mapping and transfer annex for DPA

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the intro last week. As part of our legal review for the platform pilot, legal and the DPO asked for a compact artifact set we can attach to our DPA annex. Specifically they want:

- A PII classification matrix showing which fields Redwood considers "PII" vs "non-PII" for inference payloads and telemetry.
- A diagram (or annotated flow) showing where identifying tokens are retained, pseudonymized, or redacted across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- A list of subprocessors handling tokenized or raw identifiers and whether keys are split/held by customer KMS.
- A short export/transfer playbook (if EU data crosses zones) with SLOs for evidence requests.

Could you send a single bundle (PDF + diagram + a short one-page playbook) we can attach to the DPA? Ideally by EOD Friday so our procurement review can proceed.

Attached: BioHeal_SSQ_v2.pdf (internal questionnaire)

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Miles
Senior Counsel, BioHeal

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@bioheal.com>
Cc: dpo@bioheal.com, procure@bioheal.com
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 15:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Request: PII handling mapping and transfer annex for DPA

Sarah — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble the bundle. Two quick clarifying points before we finalize: 

1) When you say "PII fields in inference payloads", do you mean user-provided prompts only, or also metadata (user_id, session_id, device_id, geo)? If you have priority fields in the SSQ, call them out and we'll highlight them.
2) For the transfer playbook: do you need an operational SLA for producing artefacts (e.g., evidence within 7 business days), or just an explanation of controls and typical timelines? Procurement sometimes needs numbers they can put in the DPA annex.

Looping in Kim and Jonas from engineering to prepare the diagram and the playbook.

Best,
Olga
Privacy and Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@bioheal.com>, dpo@bioheal.com
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:18:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: PII handling mapping and transfer annex for DPA

Olga / Jonas — initial answers below and I'm attaching an annotated drawio export (redwood-pii-annotated.drawio). High level:

- Scope for "PII fields": we recommend labeling three tiers for BioHeal's review:
  * Tier A (Direct Identifiers) — explicit identifiers that can directly identify an individual (name, email, national id, MRN).
  * Tier B (Quasi-identifiers) — session_id, device_id, IP* (IP is considered transient and only stored in logs for 7 days by default)
  * Tier C (Behavioral/Derived) — prompts and model outputs (treated as customer data; retention depends on deployment).

- Retention & pseudonymization: for Hosted API we keep prefixes in KV cache for up to 2 hours; telemetry traces retain identifiers only in hashed form and key-correlation metadata for up to 90 days. For Dedicated/Private: retention is configurable by customer; default telemetry retention is 90 days unless the customer elects shorter windows.

- Subprocessors: current primary subprocessors that may process tokenized/raw identifiers: AWS EC2/EKS (us-east-1 / eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west), FastCache Inc. (inference cache layer), and our logging provider LogStream (log ingestion). When customer-managed KMS is enabled, keys are not resident on Redwood KMS; we maintain a wrapped-key pointer only.

- Evidence SLA suggestion: 7 business days for templated artifact bundles (annotated flow, subprocessor roster, access log extracts). For privileged forensic exports we propose 20 business days. Can tighten in enterprise SLA amendments.

I've included the draw.io diagram that shows: agent -> redwood-api -> proxy -> inference cluster (KV cache, model shard) -> audit log pipeline -> long-term storage. The diagram annotates custody points and where pseudonymization occurs.

Let me know if BioHeal wants a version where IP is redacted or where we swap caching TTLs.

—Kim
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pii-annotated.drawio (diagram export)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@bioheal.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:24:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: PII handling mapping and transfer annex for DPA

Sarah / team — quick operational notes from infra that might help procurement: 

- Cross-border transfer routing: by default requests route to the nearest region to maintain latency SLOs. For BioHeal's EU tenant we can pin routing to eu-west region and enable geofencing for all inference requests (no EU->non-EU egress). That is configurable on Dedicated and Private plans and is an add-on for Hosted.
- KMS custody: for enterprise Private deployments we support a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow with HSM-backed key material. For Hosted, customers can use customer-managed KMS via our KMS proxy; in that case, Redwood only holds a wrapped key reference.
- Subprocessor proof: we can generate an export: roster.csv (subprocessor, function, region, datacenter, SOC2 evidence link) and an access_events.jsonl filtered by tenant_id for a given date range — both within the 7 business day SLA suggested by Kimberly.

Proposed next steps: I can join a 30-min call Monday to walk through the diagram and finalize the 1-page playbook. What time window works for BioHeal?

Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Miles <sarah.miles@bioheal.com>, dpo@bioheal.com, procure@bioheal.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Deliverable: PII mapping bundle + transfer playbook (draft)

Sarah — attaching the requested bundle for review. Summary of enclosed artifacts: 

1) redwood-pii-annotated.drawio — annotated dataflow (PDF export included in ZIP). Key custody points and pseudonymization gates are called out.
2) dpa-transfer-annex-draft.docx — short 1-page playbook with evidence SLAs (7 / 20 business days), optional geofencing pinning, and KMS custody options.
3) BioHeal_SSQ_v2_filled.pdf — completed questionnaire with our answers inline (we flagged three items for your DPO: IP retention policy, cache TTLs, and logging retention for tenant-scoped events).

Next steps: please confirm which fields in the SSQ you require redaction for in the public diagram and whether 7 business days for templated artifacts is acceptable. Jonas has offered a 30-minute call if you want to walk the flow.

Best,
Olga
Privacy and Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
Attachments: BioHeal_SSQ_v2_filled.pdf, redwood-pii-annotated.drawio, dpa-transfer-annex-draft.docx
